title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative: Between 2022 and 2023, the Ministry of Labour, Association of Lebanese Industrialists, and Confederation General of Lebanese workers developed a MobileApp on rights and responsibilities at work to further support skills training graduates, workers, new entrants smoothly transition to the world of work and improve the industrial relationship between employers and workers to secure and sustain decent work conditions. Since its launch in February 2023, more than 11,000 visitors used the App. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport rehabilitated six roads connecting several villages accross the country. Beirut Municipality rehabilitated its police station and approximately 5kms of sidewalks in Karanteena area, while the Lebanese Customs restored their Secretariat building in the Port vicinity as a response to the Beirut Blast. With funding from the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation and joint programme with UNICEF, the ILO strengthened the capacity of its constituents and other partners in disseminating decent work principles at national level by developing an online interactive application (web and mobile responsive) and contributing in raising awareness and skills of more than 300 officers and vulnerable trainees on rights and responsibilities at work towards ensuring job placement and employment conditions are decent. With contribution from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) through the KfW Development Bank, ILO completed 22 projects employing 7,454 workers of which 1,250 women, 3,477 Syrian and 164 person with disabilities. An active response to the Beirut blast was accomplished through 3 projects, ensuring a recovery of administrative buildings and a community recovery through sidewalks rehabilitation generating 46,190 workdays for 816 workers. ILO conducted on the job trainings for 111 workers enhancing their employability and trained local contractors on Local Recruitment Based Technologies (LRBT) and decent work practices.

Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Social Affairs rehabilitaed four Social Development Centres (SDCs) located in rural areas in the South, Akkar and Bekaa regions, with a focus on improving accessibility of people with disabilities.
By April 2023, seven municipalities in rural areas across the country had made substantial improvements to their infrastructure, generating green job opportunities and providing on-the-job trainings for their inhabitants. As a result, a total of 4,000 job opportunities were created, with 640 jobs specifically aimed at women.
Furthermore, in view of advancing a just transition to environmental sustainability in the agricultural sector, the Ministry of Agriculture, through the Lebanese Reforestation initiative, has supported 800 farmers, including 100 women, throughout the country. This result has been achieved through land reclamation, retaining walls and water reservoir building.
In April 2023, the Lebanese Mountain Trail association completed the rehabilitation of 590 kms of hiking trail passing through 50 municipalities across the Lebanese countryside based on EIIP approaches. Through the restoration of this trail network, numerous other opportunities have arisen, linking mountain villages to the trails to support sustainable tourism activities and generate employment opportunities in rural areas.
Given the challenging economic situation in Lebanon, such inter institutional and cross-sectoral cooperation and coordination is key to ensure inclusive, sustainable and resilient revitalization of rural areas through decent work. With contribution from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) through the KfW Development Bank, ILO has created employment opportunities through municipality infrastructure projects, Road Maintenance projects, Agricultural roads projects and Green Plan projects. Nineteen out of the twenty-two projects under the Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) have contributed to the improvement of rural infrastructure and to the creation of green employment in vulnerable rural areas in Lebanon.
